transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've just been feeling ever so tired, and I haven't got any energy. It's been going on for a while now.
When did you first notice it?
Hard to say exactly — it sort of crept up on me. I couldn't put a date on it.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
It's worse as the day goes on, really. Resting doesn't seem to perk me up much either.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?
Just a heavy, drained feeling, like I've got nothing left in the tank. And even after a night's sleep I don't feel refreshed.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
It's not really in one place — it's just my whole body feels flat and heavy. Nowhere specific.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?

I'm not sure how to put a number on it — it's just not too bad, but it's there all the time.

user If you had to give a rough idea — is it mild, moderate, or severe?
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
It's mostly there all the time, though some days are better than others.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?
Yes, I've noticed I get more short of breath than usual when I'm walking up hills. And a couple of friends have said I look a bit pale.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes, I've got a couple of ongoing things — my sugar, and my thyroid. I'm on tablets for both.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?
Oh, several — some tablets for my sugar and my thyroid, and something for my indigestion that I've taken for ages. And painkillers for my shoulder that I get from the chemist.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
Yes, there's one painkiller that makes me really sick — I've learned to avoid it.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
I've had to give up my swimming, which I miss. And I'm finding it harder to help my husband wash and dress in the mornings.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
I do worry, yes. My husband has Parkinson's and I look after him — I'm scared I won't be able to keep caring for him if this carries on.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
